console-unlock-guard.body:
#!/bin/bash
# Installed by build-fleet/mini-ops/ops/console-unlock-guard.sh. Tested by
# build-fleet/mini-ops/console_unlock_guard_test.py, which runs this body with stub commands; keep
# every tool call a bare name (no /usr/bin prefixes) and every path overridable, as below.
set -u
dir=${CMUX_FLEET_OPS_DIR:-/Library/Application Support/cmux-fleet-ops}
fleet=${CMUX_FLEET_DIR:-/Users/Shared/cmux-build-fleet}
pref=${CMUX_LOGINWINDOW_PREF:-/Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow}
locked_checks=${CMUX_GUARD_LOCKED_CHECKS:-3}
restart_gap_s=${CMUX_GUARD_RESTART_GAP_S:-21600}   # 6 h: one guard restart per mini, then alert
fresh_boot_s=${CMUX_GUARD_FRESH_BOOT_S:-3600}
drain_max_s=${CMUX_GUARD_DRAIN_MAX_S:-7200}   # 2 h: the most one login-window episode drains the fleet worker
state="$dir/console-unlock-guard.locked"
restarts="$dir/console-unlock-guard.restarts"
alert="$dir/console-unlock-guard.alert"
drained="$dir/console-unlock-guard.drained"   # when this episode's fleet-worker drain began (epoch)
# The fleet worker's host reservation marker (build-fleet/internal/reservation): the worker reads it
# before every claim and again after it takes host.lock, and claims nothing while it is live. The guard
# only ever writes, refreshes or removes a marker whose owner is the guard; another owner's is a
# reservation it leaves alone (and a brake).
drain_marker="$fleet/reservation.json"
drain_owner=console-unlock-guard
ours() { [ -f "$drain_marker" ] && [ ! -L "$drain_marker" ] && grep -q "\"owner\": *\"$drain_owner\"" "$drain_marker" 2>/dev/null; }
undrain() {
  if ours; then rm -f "$drain_marker" && say "fleet worker drain lifted: $1"; fi
  rm -f "$drained"
}
say() { echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) $*"; }
# Every refusal a person has to clear goes through hold: the log line alone is read by nobody.
hold() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" >"$alert" 2>/dev/null; say "$*"; exit 0; }
mkdir -p "$dir"   # a missing state dir must not silently lose the locked-check count

# --- keep the console from locking in the first place ----------------------------------------
if defaults read "$pref" autoLoginUserScreenLocked >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  defaults delete "$pref" autoLoginUserScreenLocked && say "autoLoginUserScreenLocked deleted"
fi
ds=$(pmset -g | awk '$1 == "displaysleep" {print $2}')
if [ -n "$ds" ] && [ "$ds" != 0 ]; then pmset -a displaysleep 0 && say "displaysleep $ds -> 0"; fi
# The screen saver is what locks an idle mini: loginwindow's default idle is 1200 s and the lock
# delay is 0. idleTime is a per-user ByHost pref, so it is written as the console user, in their
# session, not as root.
# The console user is the session WindowServer marks as on the physical console, not /dev/console's
# owner: that is whoever logged in last, and on a mini with hidden CI accounts logged in through its
# own Screen Sharing (fleet gui-ci-users) it named the last hidden account while the build user held
# the display (2026-11-18), so the guard muted and un-idled the wrong account. A session holds no
# nested dictionary, so each one is a flat {...}.
read_console() {
  local users
  users=$(ioreg -n Root -d1 -a | plutil -extract IOConsoleUsers json -o - - 2>/dev/null | tr -d " \t\n")
  oncon=$(printf '%s\n' "$users" | grep -o '{[^{}]*}' | grep '"kCGSSessionOnConsoleKey":true' | head -1)
  cuser=$(printf '%s\n' "$oncon" | sed -n 's/.*"kCGSSessionUserNameKey":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
  cuid=$(printf '%s\n' "$oncon" | sed -n 's/.*"kCGSSessionUserIDKey":\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p')
}
# The names the console carries when nobody is logged in on it: the login window's own session reads
# "unknown" or "loginwindow", and root is never a person. An empty name counts too. This is ci-dash's
# NO_CONSOLE_USERS (build-fleet/ci-dash/ci_dash.py); console_unlock_guard_test.py fails if the two differ.
# A CI mini on 2026-11-22 sat at the login window under an "unknown" console session, and the
# guard took "unknown" for a person: it logged "muted drift for unknown ... repair failed" every 10 min
# and never counted the login window.
no_console_users="unknown loginwindow root"
no_console_user() { [ -z "${1:-}" ] || case " $no_console_users " in *" $1 "*) true ;; *) false ;; esac; }
read_console
if ! no_console_user "$cuser" && [ -n "$cuid" ]; then
  as_console() { launchctl asuser "$cuid" sudo -u "$cuser" "$@"; }
  idle=$(as_console defaults -currentHost read com.apple.screensaver idleTime 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "${idle:-unset}" != 0 ]; then
    as_console defaults -currentHost write com.apple.screensaver idleTime -int 0 \
      && say "screen saver idleTime ${idle:-default} -> 0 for $cuser"
  fi

  # Sound is per-user on macOS. Read first so every pass reports drift, then
  # repair it in the logged-in user's Aqua session. A missing session is a
  # reportable baseline gap; the next RunAtLoad/interval pass retries it.
  audio=$(as_console osascript \
    -e 'set s to get volume settings' \
    -e 'return (output muted of s as text) & "|" & (alert volume of s as text)' 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$audio" in
    true\|0) ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$audio" ]; then
        say "muted drift for $cuser: output/alert=$audio; repairing"
      else
        say "muted drift for $cuser: output/alert unreadable; repairing"
      fi
      as_console osascript \
        -e 'set volume output muted true' \
        -e 'set volume alert volume 0' \
        || say "muted drift for $cuser: osascript repair failed"
      ;;
  esac
  beep=$(as_console defaults read -g com.apple.sound.beep.volume 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$beep" in
    0|0.0) ;;
    *)
      say "muted drift for $cuser: com.apple.sound.beep.volume=${beep:-unreadable}; repairing"
      as_console defaults write -g com.apple.sound.beep.volume -float 0 \
        || say "muted drift for $cuser: beep preference repair failed"
      ;;
  esac
  uiaudio=$(as_console defaults read -g com.apple.sound.uiaudio.enabled 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$uiaudio" in
    0|false) ;;
    *)
      say "muted drift for $cuser: com.apple.sound.uiaudio.enabled=${uiaudio:-unreadable}; repairing"
      as_console defaults write -g com.apple.sound.uiaudio.enabled -bool false \
        || say "muted drift for $cuser: UI-audio preference repair failed"
      ;;
  esac
else
  say "muted drift: no console user (${cuser:-none}); waiting for Aqua session"
fi
# A restart must not be heard across the room.
if [ "$(nvram StartupMute 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}')" != "%01" ]; then
  nvram StartupMute=%01 && say "StartupMute -> %01 (silent startup)"
fi

# --- is the console locked, or at the login window? -----------------------------------------
# Only the session on the physical console: a hidden Screen Sharing session that locks is not a
# reason to restart the mini (and the restart would end those sessions too). Hidden CI accounts are
# never on the console, so a mini with only those left is at the login window.
autologin=$(defaults read "$pref" autoLoginUser 2>/dev/null || true)
what="console locked"
if [ -n "$autologin" ] && no_console_user "$cuser"; then
  what="no session for auto-login user $autologin (login window)"
else
  case "$oncon" in
    *'"CGSSessionScreenIsLocked":true'*) ;;
    *)
      if [ -f "$alert" ]; then say "console unlocked again; clearing the alert"; fi
      undrain "the console has a session again"
      rm -f "$state" "$alert"; exit 0 ;;
  esac
fi
# A counter the guard cannot read must not stop it from ever counting again: $(( abc + 1 )) under
# set -u kills the run before it can overwrite the file, so the digits are what count.
count=$(cat "$state" 2>/dev/null)
count=${count//[!0-9]/}
n=$(( ${count:-0} + 1 ))
echo "$n" >"$state"
[ "$n" -ge "$locked_checks" ] || { say "$what ($n/$locked_checks)"; exit 0; }

# --- FileVault: a restart would stop at the unlock screen ------------------------------------
# With FileVault on there is no auto-login after a restart: the mini waits at the FileVault unlock
# screen, off the network, until a person types a password. So the guard
# restarts only a mini fdesetup says is Off; On, or an answer it cannot read, holds for a person.
case "$(fdesetup status 2>/dev/null)" in
  *"FileVault is Off"*) ;;
  *) hold "$what ($n checks); not restarting: FileVault is on (or fdesetup did not answer), so a restart would stop at its unlock screen until a person types a password. A person has to unlock this console." ;;
esac

# --- would a restart cost anyone work? -------------------------------------------------------
# Both helpers below fail closed: a python3 that cannot run reads as busy, never as free. Rebooting a
# mini out from under a reservation or a build is far worse than leaving a locked console locked.
busy=""
github_job=""
# bin[^/ ]*: a self-updated runner runs its worker from the bin.<version> directory bin links to.
pgrep -f 'bin[^/ ]*/Runner.Worker' >/dev/null && github_job=1
pgrep -x xcodebuild >/dev/null && busy="xcodebuild"
pgrep -x xctest >/dev/null && busy="xctest"
[ -n "$github_job" ] && busy="a GitHub job"
if [ -z "$busy" ] && [ -e "$fleet/host.lock" ]; then
  /usr/bin/python3 - "$fleet/host.lock" <<'PY'
import fcntl, sys
# 0: the lock is free. 3: a build holds it. Anything else is an error, and an error means busy.
with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
    try:
        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
    except OSError:
        sys.exit(3)
PY
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" = 3 ]; then busy="host.lock"
  elif [ "$rc" != 0 ]; then busy="host.lock (could not read it: python3 exited $rc)"; fi
fi
if [ -z "$busy" ] && [ -f "$fleet/reservation.json" ] && ! ours; then
  /usr/bin/python3 - "$fleet/reservation.json" <<'PY'
import json, sys, time
# Like the runner hook (glaeda_reservation.py): live when now < until. 3: the reservation expired, so
# the mini is free. 0: it is live. An unreadable or invalid file counts as reserved, and so does any
# other exit, including a python3 that is not there at all.
try:
    until = json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get("until")
except Exception:
    sys.exit(0)
sys.exit(3 if isinstance(until, int) and not isinstance(until, bool) and until <= time.time() else 0)
PY
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" = 0 ]; then busy="a reservation"
  elif [ "$rc" != 3 ]; then busy="a reservation (could not read it: python3 exited $rc)"; fi
fi
now=$(date +%s)
# kern.boottime reads "{ sec = 1792554887, usec = 684295 } Tue Oct 20 20:54:47 2026". A greedy
# ".*sec = " takes the usec, which made every uptime look like decades and the fresh-boot brake
# never hold, so minis rebooted every ~30 min. Field 4 is the seconds,
# and a boot time this cannot read refuses the restart instead of allowing it.
boot=$(sysctl -n kern.boottime 2>/dev/null | awk -F'[ ,]+' '{print $4}')
case "${boot:-}" in
  '' | *[!0-9]*) [ -z "$busy" ] && busy="kern.boottime unreadable" ;;
  *) [ -z "$busy" ] && [ "$(( now - boot ))" -lt "$fresh_boot_s" ] && busy="a restart under an hour ago" ;;
esac
# --- at the login window, drain the fleet worker so the mini can go idle ---------------------
# The busy brakes above count the work of the half of the mini that survives a logout: cmux-build-worker
# is a LaunchDaemon and kept claiming fleet jobs (package-test-lane runs xcodebuild under host.lock) back
# to back, so on two minis (2026-11-25, logout-stops-gui-launchagents.md) the brakes never cleared and the
# guard waited forever with 21/21 runners stopped. So here, past the count, with no GitHub job and no other owner's live
# reservation, the guard writes the worker's reservation marker: no new claim, running steps finish (a
# step claimed in the race goes back to the queue unrun), and a later pass finds the mini idle. It is
# written before the loginwindow restart too, so nothing is claimed in the seconds before a reboot. The
# marker's until is the first drain plus drain_max_s and never moves, so a guard that dies cannot hold
# the worker off for longer; past it the guard gives the worker the mini back for the rest of the episode
# and says so in the alert.
if [ "$what" != "console locked" ] && [ -z "$github_job" ]; then
  case "$busy" in
    "" | xcodebuild | xctest | host.lock | "a restart under an hour ago")
      since=$(cat "$drained" 2>/dev/null); since=${since//[!0-9]/}
      if [ -z "$since" ] || [ "$since" -gt "$now" ]; then since=$now; echo "$since" >"$drained"; fi
      until_s=$(( since + drain_max_s ))
      if [ "$now" -ge "$until_s" ]; then
        if ours; then
          rm -f "$drain_marker"
          printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$what ($n checks): drained the fleet worker for $(( drain_max_s / 60 ))m and the mini never went idle (${busy:-idle}); gave the worker the mini back. A person has to look at this mini." >"$alert" 2>/dev/null
          say "fleet worker drain lifted after $(( drain_max_s / 60 ))m without a heal (${busy:-idle})"
        fi
      elif [ ! -e "$drain_marker" ] || ours; then
        if ! ours; then say "$what ($n checks): draining the fleet worker (${busy:-idle}): it claims nothing new until $(date -u -r "$until_s" +%FT%TZ 2>/dev/null || echo "$until_s") or the session is back"; fi
        printf '{"schema": "glaeda-reservation/v1", "owner": "%s", "purpose": "the mini is at the login window: let it go idle so auto-login can bring the session back", "since": %s, "until": %s}\n' \
          "$drain_owner" "$since" "$until_s" >"$drain_marker.next" 2>/dev/null \
          && chmod 644 "$drain_marker.next" && mv -f "$drain_marker.next" "$drain_marker" \
          || { rm -f "$drain_marker.next"; say "could not write the fleet worker drain marker $drain_marker"; }
      fi
      ;;
  esac
fi
if [ -n "$busy" ]; then
  # A busy check that could not run leaves the guard unable to heal anything, which is a state
  # somebody has to clear; an honestly busy mini is not.
  case "$busy" in
    *"could not read it"* | *unreadable*) hold "$what ($n checks); not restarting: $busy" ;;
  esac
  say "$what ($n checks); not restarting: $busy"
  exit 0
fi

# --- at the login window, restart loginwindow before the mini ------------------------------
# A fresh loginwindow runs auto-login again, which brings the session (and every gui/501 agent) back
# without a reboot. Only a mini still at the login window after that goes on to the restart below,
# with the same 6 h bound. It runs after the busy brakes because ending loginwindow ends every session,
# including the hidden CI accounts' Screen Sharing sessions.
if [ "$what" != "console locked" ]; then
  relogin_wait_s=${CMUX_GUARD_RELOGIN_WAIT_S:-90}
  say "$what ($n checks) and the mini is idle: restarting loginwindow so auto-login runs again"
  killall loginwindow || say "restarting loginwindow failed"
  waited=0
  while :; do
    read_console
    if ! no_console_user "$cuser"; then
      rm -f "$state" "$alert"
      say "console session for $cuser is back after restarting loginwindow (${waited}s): not restarting"
      undrain "the session is back"
      exit 0
    fi
    [ "$waited" -lt "$relogin_wait_s" ] || break
    sleep 5; waited=$(( waited + 5 ))
  done
  say "still no console session ${waited}s after restarting loginwindow: falling back to a restart"
fi

# --- one restart per 6 h, then alert instead -------------------------------------------------
# $restarts is the whole bound, and it has to survive the reboot it is bounding. So a history this
# cannot read, and a restart it cannot write down, both refuse the restart: a mini whose disk is full
# would otherwise reboot every 10 minutes, which is the loop this guard exists to end.
last=""
if [ -d "$restarts" ]; then
  hold "$what ($n checks); not restarting: cannot read $restarts, so the 6 h bound is unknown"
fi
if [ -e "$restarts" ] && ! last=$(tail -1 "$restarts" 2>/dev/null); then
  hold "$what ($n checks); not restarting: cannot read $restarts, so the 6 h bound is unknown"
fi
case "$last" in
  '') ;;
  *[!0-9]*) hold "$what ($n checks); not restarting: $restarts holds something that is not a timestamp" ;;
esac
# An epoch is exactly 10 digits from 2001 to 2286. More means two lines ran together (a truncated
# write), and arithmetic on 20 digits overflows silently into a number that passes any bound; fewer
# means a truncated epoch, which reads as a restart in 1970 and would allow one more reboot.
if [ -n "$last" ] && [ "${#last}" != 10 ]; then
  hold "$what ($n checks); not restarting: $restarts holds an implausible timestamp (${#last} digits)"
fi
if [ -n "$last" ] && [ "$last" -gt "$now" ]; then
  hold "$what ($n checks); not restarting: $restarts says the last restart is in the future"
fi
if [ -n "$last" ] && [ "$(( now - last ))" -lt "$restart_gap_s" ]; then
  hold "restarted $(( (now - last) / 60 ))m ago and the console is back to \"$what\": not restarting again for $(( restart_gap_s / 3600 ))h. A person has to look at this mini (auto-login is coming back locked or not at all)."
fi
# Every restart the guard makes, newest last. The bare echo guarantees a line break, so a history
# that lost its trailing newline cannot glue two epochs into one number.
{ cat "$restarts" 2>/dev/null; echo; echo "$now"; } | grep -E '^[0-9]{10}$' | tail -20 >"$restarts.next" 2>/dev/null
mv -f "$restarts.next" "$restarts" 2>/dev/null
chmod 644 "$restarts" 2>/dev/null
if [ "$(tail -1 "$restarts" 2>/dev/null)" != "$now" ]; then
  rm -f "$restarts.next"
  hold "$what ($n checks); not restarting: could not record this restart in $restarts, so the 6 h bound would not survive the reboot"
fi
rm -f "$state" "$alert"
if [ "$what" = "console locked" ]; then
  say "console locked for $n checks and the mini is idle: restarting so auto-login starts unlocked"
else
  say "$what for $n checks and the mini is idle: restarting so auto-login brings the session back"
fi
shutdown -r now

seed-root.body:
#!/bin/bash
# Installed by build-fleet/mini-ops/ops/seed-root.sh. Keeps the CI seed root in place; see that file.
# usage: seed-root [--dry-run]    (no argument: apply, as the daemon does)
set -u
dry=0
[ "${1:-}" = --dry-run ] && dry=1
h=$(hostname -s)
base=${SEED_ROOT_BASE:-/Users/runner/_work}
leaf=cm""ux   # spelled apart: a published body names no fleet login (fleet_ops_test)
seed=$base/$leaf
marker=$seed/.cmux-seed-root
seed_2=$base/$leaf-2   # the second seed root (owned_spm_scratch.py SECOND_SEED_WORKSPACE, one level up)
fleet=${SEED_ROOT_FLEET_DIR:-/Users/Shared/cmux-build-fleet}

say() { echo "$h: $*"; }
fail() { say "skip ($*)"; exit 1; }
owner_of() { ls -ld "$1" | awk '{print $3}'; }
real_user() { [ -n "${1:-}" ] && [ "$1" != root ] && id -u "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }

user=${SEED_ROOT_USER:-}
for src in "$base" "$fleet"; do
  real_user "$user" && break
  [ -d "$src" ] && user=$(owner_of "$src")
done
real_user "$user" || user=$(ls -ld "${SEED_ROOT_CONSOLE:-/dev/console}" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $3}')
real_user "$user" || { say "skip (no runner user: $base and $fleet are not owned by one and nobody is on the console)"; exit 0; }

if [ -L "$seed" ] || { [ -e "$seed" ] && [ ! -d "$seed" ]; }; then
  say "skip ($seed is not a real directory)"; exit 0
fi
if [ -d "$seed" ] && [ ! -e "$marker" ]; then
  say "skip ($seed exists without .cmux-seed-root: another runner's tree)"; exit 0
fi
if [ -L "$base" ] || { [ -e "$base" ] && [ ! -d "$base" ]; }; then
  say "skip ($base is not a real directory)"; exit 0
fi
# The second root is left alone, with the first still kept, for the same reasons the first would be skipped.
alone_2=""
if [ -L "$seed_2" ] || { [ -e "$seed_2" ] && [ ! -d "$seed_2" ]; }; then
  alone_2="$seed_2 is not a real directory"
elif [ -d "$seed_2" ] && [ ! -e "$seed_2/.cmux-seed-root" ]; then
  alone_2="$seed_2 exists without .cmux-seed-root"
fi
note_2() { [ -z "$alone_2" ] || echo "; left alone: $alone_2"; }

if [ "$dry" = 1 ]; then
  todo=""
  [ -d "$base" ] || todo="$todo create $base;"
  [ -d "$seed" ] || todo="$todo create $seed;"
  [ -e "$marker" ] || todo="$todo write marker;"
  if [ -d "$seed" ] && [ "$(owner_of "$seed")" != "$user" ]; then todo="$todo chown $user $seed;"; fi
  if [ -z "$alone_2" ]; then
    [ -d "$seed_2" ] || todo="$todo create $seed_2;"
    [ -e "$seed_2/.cmux-seed-root" ] || todo="$todo write $seed_2 marker;"
    if [ -d "$seed_2" ] && [ "$(owner_of "$seed_2")" != "$user" ]; then todo="$todo chown $user $seed_2;"; fi
  fi
  todo=${todo# }
  if [ -z "$todo" ]; then say "ok (already in place$(note_2))"; else say "unprovisioned (would: ${todo%;}$(note_2))"; fi
  exit 0
fi

did=""
if [ ! -d "$base" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$base" || fail "cannot create $base: needs root, run via fleet-sudo"
  chown "$user" "$base" || fail "cannot chown $base to $user"
  did="$did created $base;"
fi
keep() {  # keep "$1" a directory the runner user owns, holding the marker; $2 names the marker in the line
  local root=$1 mark=$1/.cmux-seed-root
  if [ ! -d "$root" ]; then
    mkdir "$root" || fail "cannot create $root"
    did="$did created $root;"
  fi
  if [ "$(owner_of "$root")" != "$user" ]; then
    chown "$user" "$root" || fail "cannot chown $root to $user"
    did="$did chowned $root;"
  fi
  if [ ! -e "$mark" ]; then
    printf 'CI seed root: provisioned by hq build-fleet/mini-ops/ops/seed-root.sh on %s at %s\n' \
      "$h" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" > "$mark" || fail "cannot write $mark"
    chown "$user" "$mark" || fail "cannot chown $mark to $user"
    did="$did wrote $2;"
  fi
}
keep "$seed" marker
[ -n "$alone_2" ] || keep "$seed_2" "$seed_2 marker"
did=${did# }
if [ -z "$did" ]; then say "ok (already in place$(note_2))"; else say "ok (${did%;}$(note_2))"; fi

symbol-cache-cap.body:
#!/bin/bash
# Installed by build-fleet/mini-ops/ops/symbol-cache-cap.sh.
f=/System/Volumes/Data/System/Library/Caches/com.apple.coresymbolicationd/data
[ -f "$f" ] || exit 0
size=$(stat -f %z "$f")
(( size > 20 * 1000000000 )) || exit 0
rm -f "$f"
launchctl kickstart -k system/com.apple.coresymbolicationd
echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) removed $((size / 1000000000)) GB symbolication cache"
